metadata.title: About
metadata.description: What MinistryApp does: daily and monthly reports, pace against your goal, personal targets, and how your data is kept private.

hero.title: MinistryApp
hero.text: A personal record of your ministry: hours, Bible studies, and goals for the month and the service year.

install.title: Safari, then your home screen
install.text: There is nothing to download and no App Store. Open MinistryApp in Safari on your iPhone and add it to your home screen — an icon appears beside your other apps and the report opens in one tap, with no address bar in the way. Adding it only works in Safari itself, not in the browser built into Telegram, WhatsApp or another app.

day.title: Day
day.text: Log ministry hours and Bible studies for a chosen day, in 15-minute steps. Shows progress for the month and the service year.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.text: A month grid marking the days you reported. Pick a day to open its hours and studies.

month.title: Month
month.text: A day-by-day summary for the month: hours and studies in a list, compared against the goal, with the month closed off into the year.

year.title: Year
year.text: The service year (September to August), month by month: hours, deviation from the goal, and switching between years.

profile.title: Profile
profile.text: Your type of service and goal, personal monthly and yearly targets, pace status, and access to the beyond-the-goal screen.

paceDeviation.title: Pace deviation
paceDeviation.text: Every day and month is measured against the share of the goal expected by that date — green when you are ahead, terracotta when you are behind.

personalGoals.title: Personal goals
personalGoals.text: The standard hours come from your type of service; you can set your own monthly and yearly goal instead, from a preset or by hand.

beyondGoal.title: Beyond the goal
beyondGoal.text: Once the year's goal is met, a separate screen shows how many hours you are over, and in which months.

accountSignIn.title: Account sign-in
accountSignIn.text: Accounts are issued by the administrator — write to <mail>admin@jw.fenko.dev</mail> if you need one. No registration required; your report syncs across devices.

yourData.title: Your data
yourData.text: Encrypted in transit and at rest, and never passed to third parties. Only you and the super administrator can read it — not to check up on you, but so an entry can be corrected or deleted at your request.

metadata.title: Privacy & cookies
metadata.description: What MinistryApp stores about you, why it's stored, which cookies it uses, and how to access, correct, or erase your data.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.intro: This notice explains what MinistryApp stores about you and why. It covers both your personal data and the cookies and storage the app uses on your phone.

whatWeStore.heading: What we store
whatWeStore.intro: MinistryApp is a private app for recording your own ministry activity. We only store what you enter yourself — nothing is collected automatically in the background.

items.item2: The ministry entries you add by hand: date, hours, visits and any notes you write
items.item3: The monthly and yearly goals you set
items.item4: Your email address, if you joined the waitlist before the app launched
items.item5: The notification subscription your browser creates, if you chose to be told when the app launches

whatWeStore.retention: We keep your entries for as long as you use your account. If you do not sign in for six months, we delete your account and your entries with it. Ask us to delete them sooner and we will erase them within one month.

why.heading: Why we store it
why.intro: We store this data so the app can show you your own records and goals, and so you can keep a running history of your ministry activity over time.
why.waitlist: If you joined the waitlist before launch, we store that email address for one reason only: to tell you when the app is ready. We do not use it for anything else, and we delete it once the app has launched and everyone on the list has been told.
why.pushNotifications: If you chose to be told when the app launches, your browser creates a subscription: an address only it can deliver to, and two keys that encrypt what we send. We store those three values and use them for that one announcement. They let us send a notification to that browser and nothing else — we cannot read anything on your device with them. They are deleted together with your waitlist entry, and you can switch notifications off in your device settings at any time.
why.specialCategory: Because records of time spent in religious ministry reveal something about your religious beliefs, the law treats this as a special category of personal data, not ordinary personal data. We handle it with extra care and only ever with your explicit consent.
why.legalBasis: Legal basis for processing (Article 6 UK GDPR): your consent.
why.specialCategoryCondition: Special category condition (Article 9 UK GDPR): your explicit consent to us processing data that reveals your religious beliefs.
why.withdraw: You can withdraw this consent at any time, as easily as you gave it, by contacting us (see Section 6). If you withdraw consent, we will stop processing your ministry data and, if you ask us to, delete it.
why.noProfiling: We do not use your data for advertising. We do not build a profile of you. We do not use analytics or tracking tools. We do use error monitoring, which shows us what broke; it does not follow what you do or build a profile of you. We do not make automated decisions about you.

cookies.heading: Cookies and local storage
cookies.intro: MinistryApp uses one cookie, and a small amount of storage on your device to let the app work offline. Both are strictly necessary for the app to function — without them, you could not stay signed in or use the app without a network connection. Because they are strictly necessary, UK and EU cookie rules (PECR) do not require us to ask for your consent or show a cookie banner, and we do not show one.

whoCanSeeIt.heading: Who can see your data

items.you: You, when you sign in to your own account.
items.superAdmin: One super administrator, who can see account and ministry records in order to help set up accounts, correct a mistake, or delete data on request. This access is not used to monitor your activity.

whoCanSeeIt.subProcessorsIntro: Your data is stored and processed on our behalf by the following sub-processors:

subProcessors.supabase: Supabase — our database provider. Your data is stored on Supabase's managed PostgreSQL service, encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest, in the United Kingdom (London, eu-west-2).
subProcessors.vercel: Vercel — our application hosting provider, which serves the app itself.
subProcessors.sentry: Sentry — our error-monitoring provider. When the app breaks, a technical report is sent to Sentry's servers in the EU (Frankfurt, Germany): the address of the page, your browser version and the error message itself. The report does not contain your name, your email address or any ministry record, and we have switched off the collection of IP addresses.

whoCanSeeIt.dataStaysInUk: Your personal data and ministry records are stored in the United Kingdom and are not transferred outside it. The only thing that leaves is the technical error reports described above, which are processed in the EU (Frankfurt).

yourRights.heading: Your rights
yourRights.intro: Under UK and EU GDPR, you have the right to:

items.access: Access the personal data we hold about you
items.receiveCopy: Receive a copy of your data in a portable format (data portability)
items.withdrawConsent: Withdraw your consent at any time, as easily as you gave it, without affecting the lawfulness of processing before you withdrew it
items.complain: Complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) at ico.org.uk if you believe we have not handled your data properly

yourRights.contactLine: To exercise any of these rights, contact us at <mail>admin@jw.fenko.dev</mail>. We will respond within one month of your request. If your request is complex, we may extend this by a further two months, and we will tell you within the first month if we need to do this and why.

contact.heading: Contact
contact.noDpo: We have not appointed a Data Protection Officer, as this is not required at our scale. The contact details above are the single point of contact for any privacy question or rights request.

metadata.title: Sentry test
metadata.description: Debug page for checking that errors reach Sentry.

sentryExampleError.title: Sentry test
sentryExampleError.intro: Each button below causes one kind of error on purpose. Open Sentry afterwards and search for {prefix} to find them. You can mute that text there once you are done.

explicit.title: 1. Send an event
explicit.hint: Sends a handled error straight to Sentry and breaks nothing. If this one never arrives, the DSN or the tunnel route is wrong. Tagged debug_probe: true.
explicit.done: Sent. It should appear in Sentry within a minute.

handler.title: 2. Unhandled error in a handler
handler.hint: Throws inside a click handler. The global handler reports it and the page keeps working.
handler.done: Thrown. Look for an unhandled error in Sentry.

scrub.title: 3. Personal data scrubbing
scrub.hint: Sends an error whose text contains {email}. In Sentry the message should show [redacted] where the address was. If you can read the address, scrubbing is broken.
scrub.done: Sent. Check that the address is replaced by [redacted].

render.title: 4. Render error
render.hint: Throws while this screen renders. You will land on the error screen, which is the app's error boundary. Reload the page to come back.

action.title: 5. Server Action error
action.hint: Calls a Server Action that throws on the server. It should arrive in Sentry through the server request error hook.
action.done: Called. Look for a server-side error in Sentry.

serverRender.title: 6. Server Component error
serverRender.hint: Opens a page that throws while it renders on the server. You will see the error screen, and Sentry should receive a server-side error.

toast.title: 6. Backend unavailable
toast.hint: Asks Supabase for its health endpoint with a timeout too short to answer, so the call fails the way a real outage fails. The answer comes back as a state, not an exception, and the UI shows it as a toast — not a field error and not the 500 screen.
toast.button: Call a backend that cannot answer
toast.done: Called. A toast should have appeared at the top.
toast.unavailable: The backend is not responding. Please try again later.

tones.title: 7. Every toast tone
tones.hint: Shows all three tones at once, so their colours can be compared and the way the region stacks them is visible.

globalError.title: Server not responding
globalError.text: Please refresh the page in a minute.
